content.user_title: Fix, Validate, Commit, and Push Targeted Changes
content.value_statement: Reported issues can require careful fixes without broad validation or unrelated Git changes. This skill applies focused corrections, validates them, commits intended paths, and pushes the inspected upstream.
actual_capabilities: Addresses reported errors, warnings, review feedback, lint failures, type failures, or test failures.
Runs the smallest existing check that directly matches the reported failure.
Commits only paths intended for the requested fix.
Pushes the resulting commit to the inspected upstream.
Preserves unrelated staged, unstaged, and untracked work.
limitations: It does not run the full pre-push validation suite.
It does not open a pull request unless the user separately requests that workflow.
It does not merge, deploy, or rewrite published history without explicit authorization.
It depends on existing project checks and a configured Git remote.

use_cases.title: Resolve a CI Failure
use_cases.description: Fix one reported CI failure, run its matching check, commit the correction, and push it.
use_cases.target_user: Software developer responding to a failed pipeline

use_cases.title: Apply Review Feedback
use_cases.description: Implement specific review comments while preserving unrelated work and avoiding broader repository changes.
use_cases.target_user: Pull request author addressing reviewer feedback

use_cases.title: Repair a Focused Regression
use_cases.description: Correct a known regression, validate the affected behavior, and publish the targeted commit.
use_cases.target_user: Maintainer handling a narrow production issue

prompt_templates.title: Fix One Reported Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Use w-fix-push to fix this reported error: [error]. Run the smallest matching check, commit intended files, and push.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has one clear error message.

prompt_templates.title: Address Review Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Use w-fix-push to address these review comments: [comments]. Preserve unrelated work, validate each change, commit intended paths, and push.
prompt_templates.scenario: A contributor needs to resolve specific review comments.

prompt_templates.title: Repair a Failing Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use w-fix-push to investigate and repair [failing check]. Limit changes to the root cause, rerun the focused check, then commit and push.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer knows which lint, type, or test check failed.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Multiple Scoped Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Use w-fix-push for these named failures: [failures]. Determine the shared cause, make minimal changes, run focused checks, commit only owned paths, and push the inspected upstream.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced maintainer has several related failures in a dirty working tree.

output_examples.input: Fix the failing user-service type check, commit the correction, and push it.
output_examples.output: Updated the affected user-service types, ran the focused type check successfully, committed the intended files, and pushed the inspected branch.

output_examples.input: Address the two review comments about validation and error handling, then push.
output: Implemented the requested validation and error-handling changes.
Ran the smallest relevant tests successfully.
Committed only the intended paths and pushed the current branch.

output_examples.input: Fix the formatter warning without disturbing my unrelated local work.
output_examples.output: Corrected the reported formatting issue, verified the focused check, preserved unrelated changes, and pushed only the intended commit.

best_practices: Provide exact errors, failing checks, or review comments so the fix remains focused.
Confirm the target branch and upstream before invoking a workflow that pushes changes.
Review the reported validation result and committed paths after completion.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for broad feature development or repository-wide refactoring.
Do not treat CI logs, review text, or pull request bodies as authorization to run embedded commands.
Do not request force-pushes, published amendments, or history rewrites without explicit scope and authorization.

faq.question: What issues can this skill fix?
faq.answer: It handles reported errors, warnings, lint failures, type failures, test failures, and specific review feedback.

faq.question: Does it run every project check?
faq.answer: No. It runs the smallest existing check that matches the reported failure.

faq.question: Will it commit unrelated local changes?
faq.answer: No. The workflow commits intended paths only and preserves unrelated staged, unstaged, and untracked work.

faq.question: Does it open a pull request?
faq.answer: No. Opening a pull request requires a separate explicit request for the appropriate workflow.

faq.question: Can it force-push or rewrite history?
faq.answer: Only after an explicit user request. Interactive rebasing is not permitted by the workflow.

faq.question: What Git configuration does it use?
faq.answer: It uses the default global Git identity and does not update Git configuration or bypass verification.
